tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Full file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full suite: PENDING

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.

{"content":"# gh-1532 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time` in
`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` flakes red on contended CI runners
(live: fa run 38113730068, 2026-10-11).

**Root cause**: `expectLinearGrowth` (test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart)
takes a SINGLE doubling-ratio sample: one median at `baseCells` (100k ASCII
cells ≈ 3.8ms locally) and one at `2×baseCells` (≈ 7.2ms). The gate sits at
3.2x while a linear wrap measures ~2.0x — headroom of only ~1.2x on a ~4ms
baseline. On a loaded runner a single scheduler preemption or GC pause of a
few ms landing inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that one sample
past 3.2x. Timing assertions with a sub-5ms single-shot baseline are
inherently unstable on shared runners.

**Impact**: the growth-shape regression guard (the file's real purpose, per
gh-1357/gh-1496) flakes red ~1 in several hundred shard runs, blocking
unrelated PRs' Quality gates. The absolute 100ms-budget tests are unaffected
(median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers).

**Fix approach**: make the assertion hermetic, no production changes:
1. Take N=3 independent doubling attempts per growth test and assert on the
   **min** ratio — contention can only ADD wall time, so the min across
   attempts approaches the uncontended ratio; a genuine superlinear
   regression (~4x) still fails under min.
2. Assert a **lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed ~1.5x) so
   the guard stays meaningful (AC2): a degenerate flat measurement can no
   longer pass, and the retry-min cannot silently weaken the regression
   guard.
3. Thread an injectable elapsed-time clock through `medianWrapMs` /
   `expectLinearGrowth` so the contention scenario is reproduced
   deterministically in a unit test (a scripted 30ms spike on one
   measurement), instead of hoping CI scheduling reproduces it.

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh ticket (second timing-sensitive flake in
2h after gh-1528, same contended-window pattern).

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Full file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full suite: PENDING

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.

{"content":"# gh-1532 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time` in
`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` flakes red on contended CI runners
(live: fa run 38113730068, 2026-10-11).

**Root cause**: `expectLinearGrowth` (test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart)
takes a SINGLE doubling-ratio sample: one median at `baseCells` (100k ASCII
cells ≈ 3.8ms locally) and one at `2×baseCells` (≈ 7.2ms). The gate sits at
3.2x while a linear wrap measures ~2.0x — headroom of only ~1.2x on a ~4ms
baseline. On a loaded runner a single scheduler preemption or GC pause of a
few ms landing inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that one sample
past 3.2x. Timing assertions with a sub-5ms single-shot baseline are
inherently unstable on shared runners.

**Impact**: the growth-shape regression guard (the file's real purpose, per
gh-1357/gh-1496) flakes red ~1 in several hundred shard runs, blocking
unrelated PRs' Quality gates. The absolute 100ms-budget tests are unaffected
(median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers).

**Fix approach**: make the assertion hermetic, no production changes:
1. Take N=3 independent doubling attempts per growth test and assert on the
   **min** ratio — contention can only ADD wall time, so the min across
   attempts approaches the uncontended ratio; a genuine superlinear
   regression (~4x) still fails under min.
2. Assert a **lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed ~1.5x) so
   the guard stays meaningful (AC2): a degenerate flat measurement can no
   longer pass, and the retry-min cannot silently weaken the regression
   guard.
3. Thread an injectable elapsed-time clock through `medianWrapMs` /
   `expectLinearGrowth` so the contention scenario is reproduced
   deterministically in a unit test (a scripted 30ms spike on one
   measurement), instead of hoping CI scheduling reproduces it.

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh ticket (second timing-sensitive flake in
2h after gh-1528, same contended-window pattern).

{"content":"# gh-1532 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time` in
`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` flakes red on contended CI runners
(live: fa run 38113730068, 2026-10-11).

**Root cause**: `expectLinearGrowth` (test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart)
takes a SINGLE doubling-ratio sample: one median at `baseCells` (100k ASCII
cells ≈ 3.8ms locally) and one at `2×baseCells` (≈ 7.2ms). The gate sits at
3.2x while a linear wrap measures ~2.0x — headroom of only ~1.2x on a ~4ms
baseline. On a loaded runner a single scheduler preemption or GC pause of a
few ms landing inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that one sample
past 3.2x. Timing assertions with a sub-5ms single-shot baseline are
inherently unstable on shared runners.

**Impact**: the growth-shape regression guard (the file's real purpose, per
gh-1357/gh-1496) flakes red ~1 in several hundred shard runs, blocking
unrelated PRs' Quality gates. The absolute 100ms-budget tests are unaffected
(median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers).

**Fix approach**: make the assertion hermetic, no production changes:
1. Take N=3 independent doubling attempts per growth test and assert on the
   **min** ratio — contention can only ADD wall time, so the min across
   attempts approaches the uncontended ratio; a genuine superlinear
   regression (~4x) still fails under min.
2. Assert a **lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed ~1.5x) so
   the guard stays meaningful (AC2): a degenerate flat measurement can no
   longer pass, and the retry-min cannot silently weaken the regression
   guard.
3. Thread an injectable elapsed-time clock through `medianWrapMs` /
   `expectLinearGrowth` so the contention scenario is reproduced
   deterministically in a unit test (a scripted 30ms spike on one
   measurement), instead of hoping CI scheduling reproduces it.

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh ticket (second timing-sensitive flake in
2h after gh-1528, same contended-window pattern).

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

{"content":"# gh-1532 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time` in
`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` flakes red on contended CI runners
(live: fa run 38113730068, 2026-10-11).

**Root cause**: `expectLinearGrowth` (test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart)
takes a SINGLE doubling-ratio sample: one median at `baseCells` (100k ASCII
cells ≈ 3.8ms locally) and one at `2×baseCells` (≈ 7.2ms). The gate sits at
3.2x while a linear wrap measures ~2.0x — headroom of only ~1.2x on a ~4ms
baseline. On a loaded runner a single scheduler preemption or GC pause of a
few ms landing inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that one sample
past 3.2x. Timing assertions with a sub-5ms single-shot baseline are
inherently unstable on shared runners.

**Impact**: the growth-shape regression guard (the file's real purpose, per
gh-1357/gh-1496) flakes red ~1 in several hundred shard runs, blocking
unrelated PRs' Quality gates. The absolute 100ms-budget tests are unaffected
(median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers).

**Fix approach**: make the assertion hermetic, no production changes:
1. Take N=3 independent doubling attempts per growth test and assert on the
   **min** ratio — contention can only ADD wall time, so the min across
   attempts approaches the uncontended ratio; a genuine superlinear
   regression (~4x) still fails under min.
2. Assert a **lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed ~1.5x) so
   the guard stays meaningful (AC2): a degenerate flat measurement can no
   longer pass, and the retry-min cannot silently weaken the regression
   guard.
3. Thread an injectable elapsed-time clock through `medianWrapMs` /
   `expectLinearGrowth` so the contention scenario is reproduced
   deterministically in a unit test (a scripted 30ms spike on one
   measurement), instead of hoping CI scheduling reproduces it.

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh ticket (second timing-sensitive flake in
2h after gh-1528, same contended-window pattern).

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

{"content":"# gh-1532 — RCA

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time` in
`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` flakes red on contended CI runners
(live: fa run 38113730068, 2026-10-11).

**Root cause**: `expectLinearGrowth` (test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart)
takes a SINGLE doubling-ratio sample: one median at `baseCells` (100k ASCII
cells ≈ 3.8ms locally) and one at `2×baseCells` (≈ 7.2ms). The gate sits at
3.2x while a linear wrap measures ~2.0x — headroom of only ~1.2x on a ~4ms
baseline. On a loaded runner a single scheduler preemption or GC pause of a
few ms landing inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that one sample
past 3.2x. Timing assertions with a sub-5ms single-shot baseline are
inherently unstable on shared runners.

**Impact**: the growth-shape regression guard (the file's real purpose, per
gh-1357/gh-1496) flakes red ~1 in several hundred shard runs, blocking
unrelated PRs' Quality gates. The absolute 100ms-budget tests are unaffected
(median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers).

**Fix approach**: make the assertion hermetic, no production changes:
1. Take N=3 independent doubling attempts per growth test and assert on the
   **min** ratio — contention can only ADD wall time, so the min across
   attempts approaches the uncontended ratio; a genuine superlinear
   regression (~4x) still fails under min.
2. Assert a **lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed ~1.5x) so
   the guard stays meaningful (AC2): a degenerate flat measurement can no
   longer pass, and the retry-min cannot silently weaken the regression
   guard.
3. Thread an injectable elapsed-time clock through `medianWrapMs` /
   `expectLinearGrowth` so the contention scenario is reproduced
   deterministically in a unit test (a scripted 30ms spike on one
   measurement), instead of hoping CI scheduling reproduces it.

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh ticket (second timing-sensitive flake in
2h after gh-1528, same contended-window pattern).

  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key

  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Full file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full suite: PENDING

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Full file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full suite: PENDING

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Full file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full suite: PENDING

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.

    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Full file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full suite: PENDING

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Full file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full suite: PENDING

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Full file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full suite: PENDING

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Full file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full suite: PENDING

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Full file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full suite: PENDING

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.

# runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
